summary: Improper verification of cryptographic signature (CWE-347) in the firmware update handler of the...
description:
Improper verification of cryptographic signature (CWE-347) in the firmware update handler of the management service (uavmonitor_usbv1) of the 1300 communications board in DJI AeroScope Mobile (TP703) firmware 03.00.00.26, with 1300 communications board firmware 02.00.07.12 through 02.00.08.40, allows an unauthenticated attacker on the local network to install modified firmware, which gives persistent code execution as root. summary: Use of hard-coded credentials (CWE-798) on the 1300 communications board in DJI AeroScope Mobile ...

NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer. DJI has discontinued AeroScope Mobile and no fixed firmware is available.

summary: In Eclipse BaSyx Go Components versions up to and including 1.1.2, ABAC-enabled deployments of...
description:
In Eclipse BaSyx Go Components versions up to and including 1.1.2, ABAC-enabled deployments of the Submodel Repository and the AAS Environment return Submodel Elements that the caller is not authorized to read from `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}/submodel-elements`.



If an access rule grants READ on a single Submodel Element through a `$sme` `REFERABLE` object, the list route returns every element of that Submodel, including its value, as soon as one element matches the caller's rules. The single-element route and the full Submodel read enforce the same rule and deny access to the other elements. An authenticated caller with a READ grant for one element of a Submodel can therefore read all other elements of that Submodel.



The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Go Components v1.1.3.

cwes.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

summary: In Eclipse AAS4J before 3.0.1, `XmlSchemaValidator.validateSchema()` (and `AASXValidator...
description:
In Eclipse AAS4J before 3.0.1, `XmlSchemaValidator.validateSchema()` (and `AASXValidator.validateSchema()`, which calls it) validates untrusted XML with a default JAXP `Validator` that resolves external DTDs and external entities. An attacker who supplies a crafted AAS XML document or AASX package can read local files from the host, send their contents out-of-band to an attacker-controlled server, and make the validating process send arbitrary outbound requests (SSRF). Validation still returns no errors.



Details:



- Vulnerable code: `dataformat-xml/src/main/java/org/eclipse/digitaltwin/aas4j/v3/dataformat/xml/XmlSchemaValidator.java`. `schema.newValidator().validate(new StreamSource(...))` runs without `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD` / `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA` restrictions and without `disallow-doctype-decl`.



- Second entry point: `dataformat-aasx/src/main/java/org/eclipse/digitaltwin/aas4j/v3/dataformat/aasx/AASXValidator.java`. The AAS XML part of an `.aasx` package is passed unchanged to the vulnerable validator.



- `XmlDeserializer` (Jackson/Woodstox) is not affected, because DTD support is disabled by default there.



- Present since the initial import of the code base (commit `cc9da52`).



- Fix: harden the validator by setting `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD` and `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA` to `""` and rejecting `DOCTYPE` declarations. The bundled `AAS.xsd` does not need DTDs, so no functionality is lost.

summary: A directory traversal bug was discovered when unpacking 3.0 (quilt) source packages, where the...

summary: In Eclipse BaSyx Go Components versions up to and including 1.1.2, ABAC-enabled deployments of...
description:
In Eclipse BaSyx Go Components versions up to and including 1.1.2, ABAC-enabled deployments of the Submodel Repository and the AAS Environment do not apply an access rule's `FILTERLIST` fragment filters to single Submodel reads.



`GET /submodels` removes the fields that a rule's `FILTERLIST` hides, but `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}` and `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}/$metadata` return them unfiltered. An authenticated caller with READ access to a Submodel can therefore read fields that the access rules hide from them, for example `supplementalSemanticIds` keys that name the other parties allowed to read the Submodel.



If versioning is enabled (`history.mode` set to `api` or `audit`), `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}/$history` and `GET /shells/{aasIdentifier}/$history` in the Submodel Repository, AAS Repository and AAS Environment return the complete stored version without applying the rule's formula or fragment filters. A caller whose rules grant READ on these routes can read fields that the access rules hide, and Submodels and Asset Administration Shells that the direct read does not return to them at all.



The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Go Components v1.1.3.

cwes.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

summary: P-Net before 1.0.4 keeps the RPC session that is allocated for a fragment of a request with an...
description: P-Net before 1.0.4 keeps the RPC session that is allocated for a fragment of a request with an unknown activity UUID, without a timeout, when the rest of the request never arrives. A session that does not get an Application Relationship is also kept after the response. Repeated fragments or requests with different activity UUIDs exhaust the available sessions, one UDP packet per session. Once they are exhausted the device no longer answers a Connect request until it is restarted. An unauthenticated attacker with ADJACENT network access can use this to cause a denial of service.

description: P-Net before 1.0.4 does not check the number of MCR request blocks in a Connect request against the number of multicast communication relations that an Application Relationship has room for (PNET_MAX_MC_CR, 1 by default). Each further block is written past the end of the array, into the rest of the Application Relationship and, with more blocks, into the following one. The written data comes from the request. No established Application Relationship is needed, and the attacker requires ADJACENT network access. Builds with PNET_OPTION_MC_CR disabled are not affected.

cwes.name: Out-of-bounds Write

summary: P-Net before 1.0.4 finds the RPC session of a received PDU by its activity UUID only, and a...
description: P-Net before 1.0.4 finds the RPC session of a received PDU by its activity UUID only, and a reject, fault or cancel PDU for the session aborts the Application Relationship, without checking that the PDU is the answer to a call of the device or where it comes from. A host with ADJACENT network access that has observed the activity UUID of the connection, which is sent in clear in every RPC request, can abort the Application Relationship with one PDU. It also allocates a session for an unknown activity UUID and changes the address stored for an existing session.

summary: P-Net before 1.0.4 does not check the record data length of an IODWrite request to a non-user...
description: P-Net before 1.0.4 does not check the record data length of an IODWrite request to a non-user record index against the size of the record block header. The 32-bit length is reduced by the header size before it is passed to the record handlers, so a length smaller than the header underflows and the handlers receive a data length of about 65530. The fixed-size reads of the I&M and PDPort handlers can then read past the end of the session buffer. The result of the write is discarded. The attacker must have an established Application Relationship or be able to send in the context of one, and requires ADJACENT network access.

summary: P-Net before 1.0.4 releases the Application Relationship of an RPC session, without the abort...
description: P-Net before 1.0.4 releases the Application Relationship of an RPC session, without the abort procedure, when a fragment of a request has another data representation (endianness) than the first fragment of the call. The application is not told that the Application Relationship is gone, the cyclic data stops, and the resources of the Application Relationship are left referencing a cleared structure. Another host can then connect in its place. A host with ADJACENT network access that has observed the activity UUID of the connection, which is sent in clear in every RPC request, can do this with one PDU.

summary: P-Net before 1.0.4 copies the IP suite of a DCP Set request to the current and the non-volatile...
description: P-Net before 1.0.4 copies the IP suite of a DCP Set request to the current and the non-volatile configuration, and starts saving it, before the state of the device is checked. If the request is refused, for example because an Application Relationship is active, the configuration is not restored and is still saved. After a restart the device uses the refused address, and may not answer the controller or may use its address. A host with ADJACENT network access can use this while an Application Relationship is active.
